knowledgePoint.zh: 迈向更深架构的探索——VGGNet与GoogLeNet
knowledgePoint.en: The push toward deeper architectures — VGGNet and GoogLeNet

recallIntro.zh: 你走进教室，发现屏幕上显示着一张巨大的排行榜——ImageNet大规模视觉识别挑战赛的历年成绩。从2010年到2014年，错误率一路下降，红色的柱状图越来越矮。勒丘恩教授站在排行榜旁边，脸上带着一种「我早就说过」的表情。
recallIntro.en: You walk into the classroom and find the screen displaying a massive leaderboard — yearly results of the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge. From 2010 to 2014, error rates plummet steadily, the red bar chart getting shorter and shorter. Prof. LeCun stands beside the leaderboard with an 「I told you so」 expression on his face.

recallOutro.zh: 你脑海中浮现出那条不断下降的错误率曲线。从AlexNet到VGGNet到GoogLeNet，网络越来越深，错误率越来越低。一个清晰的规律正在浮现：深度就是力量。但这条路能走多远？
recallOutro.en: The plummeting error rate curve lingers in your mind. From AlexNet to VGGNet to GoogLeNet, networks grew deeper and error rates kept falling. A clear pattern was emerging: depth is power. But how far can this path go?

text.zh: 教室的三面屏幕今天都显示着同一张图：ImageNet竞赛的历年排行榜。2010年，最佳错误率28%。2011年，25%。2012年，出现了一个巨大的跳跃，降至16%。接下来的几年继续急剧下降。勒丘恩教授在白板上画了一条急速下降的曲线，然后在2012年的位置画了一颗星。
text.en: All three classroom screens display the same image today — the ImageNet competition's yearly leaderboard. 2010, best error rate 28%. 2011, 25%. 2012 — a massive jump — 16%. The following years continue dropping sharply. Prof. LeCun draws a steeply falling curve on the whiteboard and marks a star at the 2012 position.

text.zh: 2012年，一切都变了。辛顿的两个学生，克里热夫斯基和苏茨克维，用一个叫AlexNet的卷积网络赢得了ImageNet竞赛。错误率从26%一下子降到了16%，远远甩开了第二名。这并非渐进式的改进，而是一场革命。整个计算机视觉社区都被震动了。
text.en: In 2012, everything changed. Two of Hinton's students — Krizhevsky and Sutskever — won the ImageNet competition with a convolutional network called AlexNet. The error rate dropped from 26% to 16% in one shot, leaving second place far behind. This wasn't incremental improvement — it was a revolution. The entire computer vision community was shaken.

text.zh: AlexNet本质上是一个放大版的LeNet——8层深，6000万参数，处理224乘224的彩色图像，分类1000种不同的物体。它用了两个关键的新技术：在GPU上训练（计算速度提升了几十倍），以及ReLU激活函数（比传统的sigmoid更适合深层网络）。但核心架构——卷积、池化、全连接——跟我二十年前设计的LeNet一脉相承。
text.en: AlexNet was essentially a scaled-up LeNet — 8 layers deep, 60 million parameters, processing 224-by-224 color images, classifying 1,000 different objects. It used two key new techniques: training on GPUs (boosting computation speed by dozens of times) and the ReLU activation function (better suited for deep networks than the traditional sigmoid). But the core architecture — convolution, pooling, fully connected — was directly descended from the LeNet I designed twenty years earlier.

text.zh: 我要公正地说——辛顿和他的学生们做了一件非常重要的事。他们不仅证明了卷积网络能在大规模问题上工作，更重要的是，他们说服了整个社区。在AlexNet之前，大多数计算机视觉研究者还在用手工特征。AlexNet之后，几乎所有人都转向了深度学习。辛顿的勇气和坚持，我由衷地敬佩。
text.en: I must be fair — Hinton and his students did something tremendously important. They not only proved that convolutional networks can work on large-scale problems, but more importantly, they convinced the entire community. Before AlexNet, most computer vision researchers were still using handcrafted features. After AlexNet, almost everyone switched to deep learning. I sincerely admire Hinton's courage and persistence.

text.zh: AlexNet之后，一个明显的趋势出现了：大家开始尝试做更深的网络。逻辑很简单——如果8层的AlexNet这么厉害，那16层、19层甚至更深的网络会不会更厉害？2013和2014年的ImageNet竞赛给出了明确的答案。
text.en: After AlexNet, an obvious trend emerged: everyone started trying to build deeper networks. The logic was simple — if 8-layer AlexNet is this powerful, would 16-layer, 19-layer, or even deeper networks be more powerful? The 2013 and 2014 ImageNet competitions gave clear answers.

text.zh: 先说{VGGNet}——来自牛津大学的西蒙尼扬和齐塞曼。VGGNet的设计哲学简单到了极点：只用3乘3的小卷积核，一层叠一层地往深处走。VGG-16有16层，VGG-19有19层。没有花哨的技巧，就是不断重复同样的模块：3乘3卷积加ReLU，堆叠几层之后接一次池化。
text.en: Let's start with {VGGNet} — from Simonyan and Zisserman at Oxford. VGGNet's design philosophy was simple to the extreme: use only 3-by-3 convolution kernels, stacking layer upon layer going deeper. VGG-16 has 16 layers, VGG-19 has 19 layers. No fancy tricks, just endlessly repeating the same module: 3-by-3 convolution with ReLU, stack a few layers, then pool.

text.zh: VGGNet有一个巧妙的观察：两个3乘3的卷积层叠在一起，等效感受野是5乘5；三个3乘3叠在一起，等效感受野是7乘7。但参数量呢？三个3乘3的参数是3乘3乘3等于27，而一个7乘7是49。用更少的参数获得了同样大的感受野，同时每层之间还多了一个非线性激活——表达能力更强了。
text.en: VGGNet had a clever observation: two 3-by-3 convolution layers stacked together have an effective receptive field of 5-by-5; three 3-by-3 layers stacked together equal 7-by-7. But the parameters? Three 3-by-3 filters use 3 times 3 times 3 equals 27 parameters, while one 7-by-7 is 49. Fewer parameters for the same receptive field, and with an extra nonlinear activation between each layer — giving stronger expressive power.

text.zh: VGGNet选择只用3乘3的小卷积核而不是更大的滤波器。你觉得这个设计选择最大的好处是什么？
text.en: VGGNet chose to use only 3-by-3 small convolution kernels instead of larger filters. What do you think is the biggest benefit of this design choice?

text.zh: 参数更少——同样的感受野用更少的参数就能覆盖
text.en: Fewer parameters — the same receptive field can be covered with fewer parameters

text.zh: 对，参数效率是一个重要的好处。更少的参数意味着更小的过拟合风险和更低的计算成本。但我认为还有一个更深层的原因——每多加一层3乘3卷积，就多加了一个非线性变换。网络的非线性越强，能表达的函数就越复杂。三层3乘3的非线性叠加远比一层7乘7加一个非线性更加丰富。
text.en: Yes, parameter efficiency is an important benefit. Fewer parameters mean less overfitting risk and lower computational cost. But I think there's a deeper reason — every additional 3-by-3 convolution layer adds another nonlinear transformation. The more nonlinearity in the network, the more complex functions it can express. The nonlinear stacking of three 3-by-3 layers is far richer than one 7-by-7 layer with a single nonlinearity.

text.zh: 可以做得更深——小核更容易堆叠，网络可以拥有更多层
text.en: Can go deeper — small kernels are easier to stack, allowing the network to have more layers

text.zh: 这正是VGGNet的核心洞察。如果你用7乘7的大核，参数量会迅速膨胀，很难加很多层。但用3乘3的小核，每层参数很少，你可以轻松堆到16层、19层甚至更多。而我们已经看到：深度就是力量。VGGNet用最朴素的方式证明了这一点——不需要复杂的设计，只需要简单的模块和足够的深度。
text.en: That's the core insight of VGGNet. If you use 7-by-7 large kernels, the parameter count balloons quickly and it's hard to add many layers. But with 3-by-3 small kernels, each layer has very few parameters, and you can easily stack to 16, 19, or more layers. And we've already seen: depth is power. VGGNet proved this in the most straightforward way — no complex design needed, just simple modules and sufficient depth.

text.zh: 设计简洁——只有一种卷积核大小，实现和调试都更容易
text.en: Design simplicity — only one kernel size makes implementation and debugging easier

text.zh: （笑了笑）你说到了一个被低估的优点。好的工程设计应该尽可能简单。VGGNet证明了你不需要精心调整每一层的卷积核大小，全部用3乘3就够了。这种简洁让VGGNet成为了最容易理解和复现的经典架构之一。在研究中，简洁往往比复杂更有价值，因为它更容易被分析和改进。
text.en: (Laughs) You've touched on an underrated advantage. Good engineering design should be as simple as possible. VGGNet proved you don't need to carefully tune the kernel size of every layer — 3-by-3 everywhere is enough. This simplicity made VGGNet one of the most easily understood and reproduced classic architectures. In research, simplicity is often more valuable than complexity — because simple designs are easier to analyze and improve.

text.zh: VGGNet用简洁证明了深度的价值。但同一年的ImageNet竞赛上，还有另一个网络用完全不同的思路也取得了出色的成绩。
text.en: VGGNet used simplicity to prove the value of depth. But at the same year's ImageNet competition, another network achieved outstanding results with a completely different approach.

text.zh: 这就是{GoogLeNet}——谷歌的团队设计的。GoogLeNet有22层，但参数只有AlexNet的十二分之一。怎么做到的？他们发明了一种叫「Inception模块」的结构。每个模块里同时使用1乘1、3乘3和5乘5三种大小的卷积核，再加上一个池化路径，然后把所有路径的结果拼接在一起。
text.en: This is {GoogLeNet} — designed by Google's team. GoogLeNet has 22 layers, but only one-twelfth the parameters of AlexNet. How? They invented a structure called the 「Inception module」. Each module simultaneously uses 1-by-1, 3-by-3, and 5-by-5 convolution kernels, plus a pooling path, then concatenates the results of all paths together.

text.zh: Inception模块的哲学是：如果你不确定该用多大的卷积核，那就全部都用！让网络自己决定每个位置需要什么尺度的特征。有些地方可能需要精细的3乘3特征，有些地方可能需要更大范围的5乘5特征。把这个选择权交给网络，而不是由人来预设。
text.en: The Inception module's philosophy is: if you're not sure which kernel size to use, use them all! Let the network decide what scale of features each position needs. Some places may need fine-grained 3-by-3 features, others may need broader 5-by-5 features. Hand the choice to the network instead of presetting it as a human.

text.zh: GoogLeNet还大量使用了1乘1的卷积——听起来有点奇怪，对吧？一个1乘1的滤波器不看任何空间信息，它只是在通道维度上做线性组合。但这恰恰是控制计算量的关键。在做3乘3或5乘5卷积之前，先用1乘1卷积把通道数压下来，计算量就大幅减少了。这个技巧非常实用。
text.en: GoogLeNet also heavily used 1-by-1 convolutions — sounds odd, right? A 1-by-1 filter doesn't look at any spatial information; it only performs linear combinations across channels. But this is precisely the key to controlling computation. Before applying 3-by-3 or 5-by-5 convolutions, first use 1-by-1 convolution to reduce the channel count, drastically cutting computation. This trick is extremely practical.

text.zh: VGGNet追求简洁（只用3乘3），GoogLeNet追求多样性（同时用多种尺寸）。你更欣赏哪种设计哲学？
text.en: VGGNet pursues simplicity (only 3-by-3), GoogLeNet pursues diversity (multiple sizes simultaneously). Which design philosophy do you appreciate more?

text.zh: VGGNet的简洁——简单的设计更容易理解、复现和改进
text.en: VGGNet's simplicity — simple designs are easier to understand, reproduce, and improve

text.zh: 简洁确实有巨大的价值。VGGNet的影响力很大程度上来自于它的简洁——任何人都能理解它的设计，任何人都能在自己的问题上复现它。在工程实践中，一个你完全理解的简单方案往往比一个你不完全理解的复杂方案更可靠。这也是为什么VGGNet至今仍然是很多人的首选基线模型。
text.en: Simplicity has enormous value indeed. Much of VGGNet's influence comes from its simplicity — anyone can understand its design, anyone can reproduce it for their own problems. In engineering practice, a simple solution you fully understand is often more reliable than a complex solution you don't fully understand. That's why VGGNet remains many people's go-to baseline model even today.

text.zh: GoogLeNet的创新——用巧妙的设计在更少的参数下获得更好的效果
text.en: GoogLeNet's innovation — achieving better results with fewer parameters through clever design

text.zh: GoogLeNet的设计确实很巧妙。它用不到AlexNet十分之一的参数就超过了VGGNet的表现。这说明网络架构的设计本身就是一种重要的创新——不是所有的进步都来自于简单地加更多层。Inception模块引入了「多尺度并行处理」的思路，这个思想后来影响了很多后续的架构设计。
text.en: GoogLeNet's design is genuinely clever. It surpassed VGGNet's performance with less than one-tenth of AlexNet's parameters. This shows that network architecture design itself is an important form of innovation — not all progress comes from simply adding more layers. The Inception module introduced the idea of 「multi-scale parallel processing, a concept that later influenced many subsequent architecture designs.

text.zh: 两者互补——VGGNet建立了基线，GoogLeNet探索了新方向
text.en: They complement each other — VGGNet established a baseline, GoogLeNet explored new directions

text.zh: 这是最成熟的视角。科学进步需要两种人：一种把简单的事情做到极致，建立可靠的参照标准；另一种尝试全新的思路，突破已有的边界。VGGNet和GoogLeNet恰好代表了这两个方向。有了VGGNet作为简洁的基线，GoogLeNet的创新才有了评价的标尺。有了GoogLeNet的新思路，整个领域才有了新的灵感来源。
text.en: That's the most mature perspective. Scientific progress needs two kinds of people: those who push simple things to the extreme, establishing reliable reference standards; and those who try entirely new ideas, breaking existing boundaries. VGGNet and GoogLeNet represent these two directions perfectly. With VGGNet as a clean baseline, GoogLeNet's innovations have a yardstick for evaluation. With GoogLeNet's new ideas, the whole field gains new sources of inspiration.

text.zh: 不管用哪种设计，有一条规律已经非常清晰了：更深的网络表现更好。从8层的AlexNet到19层的VGGNet到22层的GoogLeNet，每次加深都带来了显著的性能提升。那么，一个自然的问题是——能不能继续加深？50层？100层？
text.en: Regardless of which design, one pattern has become crystal clear: deeper networks perform better. From 8-layer AlexNet to 19-layer VGGNet to 22-layer GoogLeNet, each increase in depth brought significant performance gains. So a natural question arises — can we keep going deeper? 50 layers? 100 layers?

text.zh: 要让网络变得更深，还需要解决一些技术障碍。其中一个重要的工具是{批量归一化}——2015年由谷歌的约菲和赛格迪提出。简单来说，它在每一层之间对数据做归一化处理，让数据的分布保持稳定。这大大加速了训练过程，也让更深的网络变得更容易训练。
text.en: To make networks deeper, some technical obstacles need to be overcome. One important tool is {batch normalization} — proposed in 2015 by Ioffe and Szegedy at Google. Simply put, it normalizes the data between each layer, keeping the data distribution stable. This greatly accelerates training and makes deeper networks much easier to train.

text.zh: 但即使有了批量归一化，当网络深到一定程度，比如超过30层，一个奇怪的现象出现了：网络的表现不升反降。问题并非过拟合，因为训练集上的表现也在变差。更深的网络居然比浅一点的网络更差？这不应该啊。一个56层的网络至少应该不比20层的差，最坏情况下，多出的36层什么都不做就行了嘛。
text.en: But even with batch normalization, when networks get deep enough — say, beyond 30 layers — a strange phenomenon appears: performance gets worse, not better. It's not overfitting — performance on the training set also degrades. Deeper networks are actually worse than shallower ones? That shouldn't happen. A 56-layer network should at least be no worse than a 20-layer one — in the worst case, the extra 36 layers could just do nothing.

suggestedContent.zh: 2012年后卷积网络的三大里程碑：(1) AlexNet (8层) 用GPU训练+ReLU激活，错误率从26%降到16%，引爆深度学习革命；(2) VGGNet (16/19层) 只用3x3卷积核，用最简洁的设计证明了深度的价值；(3) GoogLeNet (22层) 用Inception模块实现多尺度并行处理，参数量极少。规律：更深=更好。
suggestedContent.en: Three milestones in CNNs after 2012: (1) AlexNet (8 layers) with GPU training + ReLU, error rate from 26% to 16%, triggering the deep learning revolution; (2) VGGNet (16/19 layers) using only 3x3 kernels, proving depth's value with minimal design; (3) GoogLeNet (22 layers) using Inception modules for multi-scale parallel processing with very few parameters. Pattern: deeper = better.

text.zh: 更深的网络反而表现更差——这个「退化问题」说明了什么？
text.en: Deeper networks actually perform worse — what does this 「degradation problem」 tell us?

text.zh: 优化太难了——梯度在这么多层中传播会出现问题
text.en: Optimization is too hard — gradients face problems propagating through so many layers

text.zh: 你触及了问题的核心。这是一个优化问题。理论上深层网络的表达能力严格强于浅层网络，但反向传播在穿越几十层的时候，梯度信号要么变得极小（梯度消失），要么变得极大（梯度爆炸）。网络虽然有能力学到好的解，但优化算法找不到那个解。这就好像一座山里有金矿，但你的地图不够精确，怎么走都走不到。
text.en: You've touched the heart of the problem. It's an optimization issue. Theoretically, deep networks have strictly greater expressive power than shallow ones, but as backpropagation traverses dozens of layers, gradient signals either become vanishingly small (gradient vanishing) or explosively large (gradient exploding). The network has the capacity to learn a good solution, but the optimization algorithm can't find it. It's like knowing there's gold in a mountain, but your map isn't precise enough to get there.

text.zh: 多出的层连「什么都不做」都学不会——恒等映射不容易优化
text.en: The extra layers can't even learn to 「do nothing」 — identity mapping is hard to optimize

text.zh: 非常精辟的观察！这正是何恺明后来提出的关键洞察。用标准的卷积层学习恒等映射，也就是「输入什么就输出什么」，对优化器来说其实很困难。你需要每个权重恰好取到特定的值才能实现恒等映射。如果有一种方法能让「什么都不做」变成默认行为，那额外的层就不会有害了。这个想法直接催生了下节课的主题。
text.en: A very astute observation! This is precisely the key insight He Kaiming later proposed. Learning an identity mapping — 「output exactly what comes in」 — with standard convolution layers is actually hard for optimizers. Every weight needs to take a specific value to achieve identity mapping. If there were a way to make 「do nothing」 the default behavior, extra layers would never be harmful. This idea directly led to next lesson's topic.

text.zh: 也许网络不是越深越好——达到某个深度后收益递减
text.en: Maybe deeper isn't always better — there are diminishing returns beyond a certain depth

text.zh: 如果这个推理是对的，那么深度学习就撞上了天花板。但后来的研究证明——深度的收益并没有真正消失，只是我们没有找到正确的方法来训练这么深的网络。退化问题是我们训练方法的限制。一旦找到解决方案，100层、甚至1000层的网络都能成功训练。下节课你就会看到这个解决方案。
text.en: If this reasoning were correct, deep learning would have hit a ceiling. But later research proved — the benefits of depth didn't truly vanish; we just hadn't found the right way to train such deep networks. The degradation problem isn't a limitation of depth itself, but of our training methods. Once the solution was found, networks with 100 or even 1,000 layers could be successfully trained. You'll see this solution next lesson.

text.zh: 退化问题是2014年到2015年间最令人困扰的难题。大家都知道更深应该更好，但实验结果就是不合作。这个谜题的解答，来自一个简单到令人拍案叫绝的想法——下节课，我们来揭晓。
text.en: The degradation problem was the most perplexing puzzle from 2014 to 2015. Everyone knew deeper should be better, but the experimental results just wouldn't cooperate. The answer to this puzzle came from an idea so simple it's breathtaking — next lesson, we'll reveal it.

suggestedContent.zh: 退化问题：当网络深度超过约30层时，训练和测试错误率都反而上升。原因是优化困难——标准卷积层难以学会恒等映射（即「什么都不做」）。这意味着更深的网络无法至少复制浅层网络的表现。批量归一化缓解了部分问题，但无法根本解决退化。
suggestedContent.en: Degradation problem: when depth exceeds ~30 layers, both training and test errors increase. Not overfitting — it's optimization difficulty — standard convolution layers struggle to learn identity mapping (「do nothing」). This means deeper networks can't even replicate the performance of shallower ones. Batch normalization alleviates the problem partially but doesn't fundamentally solve degradation.

text.zh: 勒丘恩教授在白板的急降曲线末端画了一个大大的问号，然后转向大家。「从8层到19层到22层，我们走得越来越深。但前方有一堵墙——退化问题。要突破这堵墙，我们需要的是一个更巧妙的方法。下节课见。」他收起马克笔，带着一个意味深长的微笑离开了教室。
text.en: Prof. LeCun draws a large question mark at the end of the plummeting curve on the whiteboard, then turns to the class. 「From 8 layers to 19 to 22, we've been going deeper and deeper. But there's a wall ahead — the degradation problem. To break through, we don't need a bigger hammer, but a cleverer approach. See you next lesson」. He caps his marker and leaves with a meaningful smile.
